spiritual_reading.full_translation:
Divine love is the origin of all greatness, abiding in its own splendor in the inmost blessedness of life. In that inmost, the whole Divine is made manifest; for the Divine and the love that proceeds from it are one living reality, not divided but united as a single form. This is so because the Divine gives itself wholly to all that can receive, being present in every ordered extension of heaven and in every faculty that lives from it. Therefore the Divine is named the Lord of all things as love itself, since from love comes all power of overcoming evil, and from love comes the strengthening and preserving of the entire heavenly communion and of every power within it.

Opposed to this, hatred is the first state of spiritual death that arose, and from it the entire domain of falsity and denial was opened. It is called hatred because it lays waste everything that is born from its own condemnation; it even transgresses its proper bounds and assaults a good outside its own nature, and brings it to ruin. Therefore it is called accursed, because it works destruction by injuring the life of the will and by profaning what it has no right to claim.

Even now it continues to inflict harm and devastation in every form of natural life. It extinguishes life by many kinds of spiritual death, which are evident today in every operation and in every manner of life. It also assaults and seeks to extinguish the saving Divine truth and the living spiritual life that ought to be joined to it, just as it did from the beginning. Therefore it is named from what is accursed, and from its own envy and adversarial spirit, and from its own evil, because it is the same perverted love multiplying itself in every degree.

paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS the positive pole by stating love as the Divine origin and the source of all preservation and victory.

paragraph_translations.translation: Opposed to this, hatred is the first state of spiritual death that arose, and from it the entire domain of falsity and denial was opened. It is called hatred because it lays waste everything that is born from its own condemnation; it even transgresses its proper bounds and assaults a good outside its own nature, and brings it to ruin. Therefore it is called accursed, because it works destruction by injuring the life of the will and by profaning what it has no right to claim.
paragraph_translations.connection: SHIFTS from Divine love to its opposite, describing the origin and character of spiritual death.
paragraph_translations.notes: “A power foreign to it” is taken as a good outside hatred’s proper sphere; the exact quality of that power is not specified.

paragraph_translations.translation: Even now it continues to inflict harm and devastation in every form of natural life. It extinguishes life by many kinds of spiritual death, which are evident today in every operation and in every manner of life. It also assaults and seeks to extinguish the saving Divine truth and the living spiritual life that ought to be joined to it, just as it did from the beginning. paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES the negative pole by extending hatred’s action into the present and naming its reproducing forms.
paragraph_translations.notes: The paired phrases about being named “from the hated… from the envy… from the devil… from the bad” compress into one idea: evil generates like evil; specific distinctions among the terms are not fully recoverable from the paragraph alone.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Coherent and strongly dual-structured: it defines Divine love as the one living source that gives itself universally, then contrasts hatred as the first spiritual death that opens falsity and multiplies destruction. The voice is consistent; the only mild compression is in the final list of names, which functions more as cumulative reinforcement than as distinct new steps.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential teaching: love is defined by what it does (self-giving, revealing, granting victory), and the metaphysics (one living body) arises from that function. No narrative break or jurisdictional inventory appears.
findings.evidence: Text: “Love is the Father of Greatness… The entirety of the divine has been revealed… These two are a single living body… because he has given himself for every thing… they called the Father… ‘love’. For he gave the victory to his aeons and his limbs.” The spiritual reading does not stumble here; it tracks the functional logic (self-gift → universal presence → victory/preservation) without forcing alien categories.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential contrast: hate is defined as a functional/ontological principle (“first death”) that generates a realm (“revealed the land of darkness”) and destroys even what is outside its proper sphere. The only difficulty is genuine semantic under-specification (“a power foreign to it”), not a sign of insertion.
findings.evidence: Text: “Hate is the first death that welled up. It revealed the land of darkness… it has ruined all its perdition’s offspring; it sinned even against a power foreign to it, and ruined it.” The reading notes: “A power foreign to it… the exact quality… is not specified.” That is precisely a lexical/interpretive gap, but the paragraph remains a single functional description (hate as destructive, transgressive death), with no administrative markers (no ranks, stations, named governors, inventories). Removing any clause would not improve flow; the logic is already continuous (origin → realm disclosed → destructive character → reason for name).

findings.diagnosis: Mostly clean correspondential continuation with a minor rhetorical expansion: the present-tense extension (“today again… today…”) and the climactic string of epithets (“hated… envy… devil… bad”) intensify rather than redirect the teaching. The spiritual reading’s ‘compression’ is a genuine rhetorical pile-up, not an administrative overlay.
findings.evidence: Text: “Today again it causes wounding… It kills them all with diverse deaths… Even the Cross of Light, the living soul… Indeed… they called it ‘hated’… the envy… the devil… the bad…” The reader notes the only stumble: “paired phrases… compress into one idea… specific distinctions… not fully recoverable.” That is exactly what we expect from an emphatic synonym-chain: multiple names for the same destructive function, not a list of officials/jurisdictions. Crucially, “Cross of Light, the living soul” participates in the same functional story (hate ‘kills/ruins’ life and light) and does not introduce governance taxonomy.

textual_criticism.summary: No textual-critical disruptions detected. All paragraphs are in a consistent correspondential (functional) voice with tight dual structure (love vs hate). The only stumbles in the spiritual reading are genuine difficulties: (1) an under-specified referent in ¶4 (“a power foreign to it”), and (2) a rhetorical synonym-chain in ¶5 that invites compression. Recommendations: none (0 excisions, 0 annotations).

harmonized_paragraphs.text: ⟨p.156⟩Love is the Father of Greatness, who dwells in his glorious land. The entirety of the divine has been revealed [therein]in! These two are a single living body, the Father and his love; because he has given himself for every thing, as he exists in his aeons. Indeed, due to this, they called the Father, the Lord of the totality, 'love'. For he gave the victory to his aeons and his limbs.

Hate is the first death that welled up. It revealed the land of darkness. This one called 'hate', because it has ruined all its perdition's offspring; it sinned even against a power foreign to it, and ruined it. Due to this they shall call it 'hated'; for it has caused destruction, both wounding in flesh, and what is not its own.

Today again it causes wounding and destruction in all flesh. It kills them all with diverse deaths; these that are displayed today in every thing, in every type. Even the Cross of Light, the living soul, likewise too it ruins and kills them; as it did at the start. Indeed, due to this have they called it 'hated', this one from the hated; the envy from the envy; the devil from the devil; the bad that came about from the bad.

changes_summary: No changes made. All findings (¶2, ¶4, ¶5) carried a recommendation of none; therefore no excisions or other edits were applied.
